To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a low-cost vision system can be used to detect doorways, which is useful for visually impaired people; 2) a low-cost system can be used for centre-path travel in urban environments, which is useful in the same way; 3) both of the above are achieved by a low cost vision system using sparse vision; 4) the algorithms used are robust to changes in lighting conditions and the appearance of the scene.
we have developed an inexpensive, low-cost vision system that can provide visually impaired users with the ability to detect doorways as well as navigate along a centre-path.
We describe algorithms for doorway and path detection that use a single camera and sparsely sampled images.
